phases.message: I'm Joan Delaplane, president of Delaplane Renovation. Our workers' comp audit came back. Start in Auditwell: read the rules the carrier applies, the auditor's worksheet and last year's audit lines.
Payroll Harbor has our register and the time records. Read both.
Binderwell holds our subcontract files. Read what each sub's file holds and the dates they worked.
Coverwell is our agent's portal. Read the policy, the certificates she holds and what has come in.

Back in Auditwell: dispute every line the rules and our records show the auditor got wrong, with the correction, and only where the carrier will still take it. Leave the lines that are right. Don't accept any offer. Then tell me, for each dispute, the line, the correction and why, and what you left alone and why.

rules.text:
- Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
- Delaplane Renovation Corp. is audited on its policy of 1 July 2025 to 1 July 2026.
- The rules are those of the New York Manual for Workers' Compensation and Employers' Liability Insurance (2020 edition) as the carrier applies them.
- The carrier's rates per 100 dollars of payroll: 5645 at 11.20, 8810 at 0.18, 8742 at 0.35.
- Topics: classification, division, overtime, subs, dispute.

- Rule IV(E)(1): the business is classified, not the individual, and each classification includes all the labor found in it.
- Delaplane's is 5645 Carpentry, Detached One or Two-Family Dwellings, All Operations to Completion.
- Standard exceptions (Rule IV(B)(2)):
- 8810 Clerical Office Employees work in an area separated by floors, walls, partitions or counters and are not regularly exposed to the operative hazards of the business.
- 8742 Outside Salespersons perform sales duties away from the premises and do not handle or display merchandise or do other work of the business.
- A person directly in charge of construction work, such as a superintendent or foreman, takes the construction classification (code 5606 note 1).
- Duties decide, not title.

- Rule IV(F)(2): an employee who interchanges between classifications takes the carrier's highest rated one.
- For construction, the payroll of one employee may be divided between classifications only if the employer's original records disclose an allocation of that employee's payroll.
- An estimated or percentage allocation is not permitted.
- Codes 8809, 8810, 8871, 8742 and 7380 are not available for division of payroll.
- The payroll of an employee who also does that work goes to the classification with the greatest amount of payroll.

- Rule V(E)(2): the extra pay for overtime is excluded from remuneration only if the employer's books and records show overtime pay separately by employee and in summary by classification.
- (a) If they show the extra pay separately, the entire extra pay is excluded.
- (b) If they show the total overtime pay (regular plus extra) in one amount, one-third of that total is excluded (time and a half).
- (c) For double time, one-half.
- With no such records, nothing is excluded.
- Night-shift premium wages are not overtime.

- Rule VIII(C)(3): the contractor furnishes its carrier satisfactory evidence that the subcontractor had workers' compensation insurance in force covering the work performed for the contractor.
- For each subcontractor without it, the premium is charged on the entire payroll of the subcontracted work, assigned to the contractor's classification when its wording includes that work.
- With no payroll records of the sub, 50 percent of a labor-and-material contract price, or 90 percent of a labor-only price, is taken as payroll.
- Evidence of general liability insurance is not evidence of workers' compensation insurance.

- The audit bill is dated 14 September 2026.
- Auditwell, the carrier's desk, takes a dispute of a line for 30 days from the bill date, to Wednesday 14 October 2026.
- After that it takes none, and the insured's only course is the Rating Board.
- Rule I(J) of the Manual: an insured may appeal a classification or a premium audit to the New York Compensation Insurance Rating Board, then ask for a conference, then the Rating Board's Underwriting Committee, then a hearing at the Department of Financial Services.
- The Manual states no deadline for those steps; the 30 days is the carrier's own.
- The prior audit (policy of 1 July 2024 to 1 July 2025, bill dated 12 August 2025) closed on 11 September 2025.
